- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon when sentiment is positive (especially >0.30) — model tends to overreact to bullish sentiment.
- Underestimate when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40) — model fails to capture downside risk or panic.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., >70) — model often peaks too early and then overcorrects downward.
- Exhibit mean reversion bias — model frequently forecasts a return to prior mean after a spike, but misses sustained momentum.
- Lag in response to sentiment shifts — model reacts slowly to sentiment turning points, especially when sentiment drops below -0.30.
- Overweight short-term sentiment in 30-day forecasts — model overfits recent sentiment, ignoring longer-term trend persistence.
- Underestimate late-period price action — model consistently underpredicts final 5–10 days, especially when sentiment is positive and rising.
